lessons.Lesson: Standing roles resolve; capitalised unknown names do not
lessons.Current text: A descriptive definite that names a kind of thing but not which one ("the Bitcoin ETF", "the major-bank stablecoin consortium", "the open-access version", "the infrastructure", "the new model") makes the claim Context-dependent: the reader must already know which ETF, consortium, version or product is meant. Applies to countable things, not to abstract or mass nouns ("the regulatory clearance", "the market").
lessons.Proposed text: A descriptive definite that names a kind of thing but not which one ("the Bitcoin ETF", "the major-bank stablecoin consortium", "the open-access version", "the infrastructure", "the new model") makes the claim Context-dependent: the reader must already know which ETF, consortium, version or product is meant. A capitalised, name-like phrase for a body that readers do not know is still such a kind. A group that every reader knows by its standing role (such as a press pool) counts as identified. Applies to countable things, not to abstract or mass nouns ("the regulatory clearance", "the market").
